hypothesis: H1 (ensemble benefit): For enterprise voice-cloning detection in customer service audio, well-calibrated ensembles that combine heterogeneous detectors (signal-level supervised models, self-supervised representations, and heuristic/metadata features) will achieve a strictly better operating curve (ROC/PR), with lower business-relevant false negative rates at fixed false positive rates, than any individual detector configured in isolation.

H2 (domain adaptation): Lightweight domain adaptation (fine-tuning or calibration on small in-domain samples for new languages/accents/channels) will recover a substantial fraction of the baseline-domain performance (e.g., ≥70% of AUC/EER gap) relative to non-adapted detectors when evaluated on mismatched conditions typical of enterprise deployments.

H3 (cost-aware optimization): When cost (latency, compute, licensing) is explicitly incorporated into model selection and fusion rules, enterprises can identify ensemble configurations that are Pareto-efficient—dominated neither in detection quality nor in cost—relative to naive 'strongest model only' or 'everything everywhere' strategies.

baseline.description: Single-model baseline synthetic vs. human voice detector as implemented in Chapter 5: a supervised signal-level classifier deployed as a service, trained and evaluated on a base-domain dataset of English, narrowband (8 kHz) customer-service-style audio.

detectors.implementation: Convolutional neural network over log-Mel spectrograms or MFCCs with a sigmoid output for synthetic vs. human classification.
detectors.training_data: Base-domain dataset D_base (e.g., curated from public synthetic voice corpora plus matched human speech segments) as defined in the Chapter 5 pipeline.
detectors.inference_interface: HTTP/REST API service (Docker container) exposing /predict that returns p_synth for each audio segment.
detectors.expected_operating_point: Threshold τ_base selected on a held-out validation split of D_base to achieve a business-defined trade-off (e.g., target FAR/FRR or EER) as in Chapter 5.

datasets: D_base_test: Held-out test partition (same language/accent/channel as training).
D_new_lang: Different language (e.g., Spanish or another non-English language) with similar channel conditions, including synthetic and human speech.
D_new_channel: Same language as D_base but different telephony-like channels (e.g., VoIP compression, mobile recordings, background noise).
D_adv_tools: Synthetic voices generated using a set of contemporary voice cloning tools not seen during training (different architectures/providers).

treatment.description: Multiple detection strategies and ensembles evaluated within a shared experimental harness that standardizes datasets, preprocessing, metric computation, and cost analysis.

detectors.notes: Incremental variant of the baseline CNN with tuned architecture/regularization but same input features and training data; serves as a supervised comparator.
Self-supervised speech representation model (e.g., wav2vec-style or HuBERT-style backbone) frozen or lightly fine-tuned, followed by a small supervised classifier trained on D_base.

Simple feature and rule-based detector using non-neural cues such as spectral flatness anomalies, pitch/energy statistics, jitter/shimmer proxies, detection of known watermarking patterns when present, and call metadata (e.g., ASR confidence, call path) when available.
Optional integration with a vendor-provided synthetic voice classifier via API, where licensing costs are modeled; used where organizational policies allow.

ensembles.description: Binary hard-voting ensemble that thresholds each component detector to synthetic/human using per-detector validation-tuned thresholds, then applies majority vote to yield a final label.
Weighted average of calibrated synthetic probabilities from each component detector, with weights learned on a validation set to optimize a specified objective (e.g., minimize FNR at 1% FPR).
ensembles.constraints: Weights must be non-negative and sum to 1. External detector may be omitted if unavailable; ensure configuration files clearly document active components.

ensembles.description: Meta-classifier (e.g., logistic regression or gradient-boosted tree) trained on out-of-fold predictions and side-channel features (e.g., channel type) from base detectors to produce final synthetic probabilities.
ensembles.training_protocol: K-fold cross-validation over D_base_train to obtain unbiased out-of-fold predictions for meta-learner training.

ensembles.description: Decision rule that fuses detector scores with business context (call risk tier, transaction amount, customer segment) to implement tiered thresholds and fallback behaviors.
policy_examples: Low-risk: Use single fast detector (baseline_cnn_mfcc) with relaxed threshold.
Medium-risk: Require agreement between baseline and self-supervised detectors for 'human' decision; disagreement triggers agent review.
High-risk: Default to 'suspected synthetic' unless strong evidence from both models supports 'human' plus additional verification factors.

domain_adaptation_strategies.description: Fine-tune supervised and self-supervised-based detectors using a small labeled sample from new-language dataset D_new_lang_train while freezing early layers to mitigate overfitting.
domain_adaptation_strategies.data_budget: e.g., 5–20 hours total labeled audio per condition, stratified across synthetic/human and key accents.

domain_adaptation_strategies.description: Do not change model weights; instead, recalibrate decision thresholds or apply temperature scaling on D_new_channel_val to restore desired FPR/FNR trade-offs.
domain_adaptation_strategies.data_budget: e.g., 500–2,000 short segments per channel type.

domain_adaptation_strategies.description: Optional: Use unlabeled in-domain audio (mixed synthetic likelihood) to adapt normalization layers or feature statistics (e.g., CMVN) without labels.
domain_adaptation_strategies.data_budget: e.g., 50–100 hours unlabeled, where accessible under privacy policies.

adversarial_evaluation.description: Stress-testing all detectors and ensembles using audio generated from a curated set of known voice cloning tools and parameter settings.
attack_parameters: Variation in cloning data duration (few seconds vs. minutes).
Variation in synthesis text complexity and prosody.
Post-processing: noise injection, codec changes, mixing with background audio, replay through real telephony paths where feasible.

cost_aware_configs.description: Use only baseline_cnn_mfcc with optimized batching and CPU-only inference; intended for large-volume, lower-risk call flows.
cost_aware_configs.constraints: Latency_p95 per 10s audio must remain under an enterprise-defined target (e.g., 200 ms) and infrastructure cost must be minimized.

cost_aware_configs.description: Use ensemble_stacking_meta_lr plus external_api_detector for high-risk transaction flows, accepting higher compute and licensing costs.
cost_aware_configs.constraints: Latency_p95 per 10s audio must remain under a stricter target (e.g., 500 ms), and cost per 1k minutes must be explicitly measured.

workloads.description: Evaluation on base-domain test set D_base_test using identical pre-processing across all detectors in the harness.

channels: simulated or real contact center narrowband telephony (8 kHz).
data_characteristics.segment_length: Short segments (e.g., 3–15 seconds) sampled from longer calls; segment-level labels assigned based on dominant content.
data_characteristics.size: Sufficient for statistically stable ROC and PR curves (e.g., at least several thousand segments per class).

workloads.purpose: Quantify improvements of individual detectors and ensembles over the Chapter 5 baseline under in-domain conditions.

workloads.description: Cross-language generalization evaluation using D_new_lang before and after application of domain adaptation strategies.

languages: Non-English language(s) relevant to the intended deployment, such as Spanish, Portuguese, or others.
channels: Similar telephony or VoIP conditions as D_base where possible.
data_characteristics.segment_length: Comparable to WL1 for comparability of metrics.
data_characteristics.size: Adequate to compute stable AUC/EER and FNR@FPR estimates; class balance should be approximately even or documented.

workloads.purpose: Test hypothesis H2 by measuring performance drop due to language shift and the degree to which adaptation closes the gap.

workloads.description: Channel-mismatched evaluation using D_new_channel, including mobile, VoIP, and potentially noisy environments.

languages: Same as D_base to isolate channel effects where feasible.
channels: Mobile network codecs, VoIP with varying jitter/packet loss, on-premise PBX, and other relevant paths.
data_characteristics.size: Sufficient volume across channel types to allow per-channel metric reporting.

workloads.purpose: Evaluate channel robustness of detectors and ensembles, and compare calibration-based vs. weight-updating adaptation under typical enterprise telephony diversity.

workloads.description: Adversarial stress-testing using D_adv_tools generated from multiple cloning tools and post-processing chains.

languages: At least the primary supported languages in enterprise deployments; prioritize English plus one additional language if possible.
channels: Include 'clean' synthetic outputs and versions post-processed through actual or emulated telephony chains.
data_characteristics.segment_length: May include both short prompts and longer conversational excerpts; record length distributions.
data_characteristics.size: Enough diversity across tools and parameterizations to prevent overfitting detectors to a single cloning pattern.

workloads.purpose: Assess resilience of detection strategies and ensembles against realistic adversary capabilities; probe for systematic blind spots.

workloads.description: Throughput and latency benchmarking for selected configurations (baseline and ensembles) under realistic call-volume simulations.

languages: Mix reflecting actual call distributions where possible.
channels: Representative mix of channels present in target deployment.
data_characteristics.labels: Not required for pure latency/cost measurement; any previously used evaluation audio may be reused.
data_characteristics.segment_length: Distributions approximating real average talk times and chunk sizes used in streaming setups (e.g., 1–5 second buffers).
data_characteristics.size: Large enough to saturate system under expected peak concurrency (e.g., tens of thousands of segments).

workloads.purpose: Quantitatively estimate latency, resource utilization, and approximate cost for multiple detector and ensemble configurations to support cost-benefit trade-off analysis.

randomness: Set and log global random seeds for all frameworks used (e.g., Python, NumPy, PyTorch/TF, any gradient boosters).
Ensure deterministic data shuffling and split generation by storing and versioning split indices (train/val/test) instead of regenerating on each run.
Use fixed cross-validation folds for stacking meta-model training and preserve them in configuration files under version control.
data_handling: Use immutable dataset manifests referencing exact audio files and checksums; store under version control or a data registry.
Standardize pre-processing steps (resampling, mono conversion, normalization, feature extraction) across detectors where applicable and document any detector-specific divergences.
Ensure that no speaker, call, or cloning session appears in both training and test splits to avoid leakage, particularly for adversarial datasets.
Explicitly separate data used for domain adaptation (fine-tuning or calibration) from held-out domain test sets.
evaluation_protocol: Implement a single, shared evaluation harness that all detectors and ensembles plug into, responsible for loading datasets, running inference, computing metrics, and logging results.
Run all models on the same hardware profile when comparing latency and throughput; document CPU/GPU model, memory, and concurrency settings.
For each configuration, perform at least N_rep repetitions (e.g., 3–5) of latency benchmarking to account for variability; report median and dispersion (e.g., IQR or standard deviation).
Use consistent segment-level decision rules and aggregation strategies (if aggregating to call-level metrics) across detectors and ensembles.
hyperparameters: Maintain a central configuration file (e.g., YAML) listing hyperparameters for each detector and ensemble, checked into the repository.
Perform hyperparameter tuning on validation sets only; avoid peeking at test performance when selecting hyperparameters.
For ensembles, lock the fusion weights, voting rules, or meta-model parameters after validation; do not adjust based on test set results.
governance_and_compliance: Before using any real customer audio, ensure compliance review and necessary approvals; where possible, rely on anonymized or synthetic training/evaluation datasets.
Ensure that any integration with third-party or proprietary detectors complies with licensing terms and data-processing agreements.
Document the provenance and licensing of all datasets and tools, particularly adversarial voice cloning tools, in a separate manifest.

metrics.name: AUC_ROC
metrics.description: Area under the receiver operating characteristic curve computed over segment-level synthetic vs. human classification scores.

metrics.name: AUC_PR
metrics.description: Area under the precision–recall curve; especially informative when synthetic segments are rare relative to human segments.

metrics.name: EER
metrics.description: Equal error rate at the operating point where false acceptance and false rejection rates are equal.

metrics.name: FNR_at_1pct_FPR
metrics.description: False negative rate (synthetic misclassified as human) when threshold is chosen to yield approximately 1% false positive rate on validation data.

metrics.name: FNR_at_5pct_FPR
metrics.description: False negative rate at approximately 5% false positive rate; provides insight into behavior at a more permissive operating point.

metrics.name: Latency_p50
metrics.unit: milliseconds per standardized audio unit (e.g., per 10 seconds equivalent)
metrics.description: Median per-sample inference latency measured end-to-end within the harness, including I/O and pre-processing.

metrics.name: Latency_p95
metrics.unit: milliseconds per standardized audio unit (e.g., per 10 seconds equivalent)
metrics.description: 95th percentile per-sample inference latency; important for real-time call handling SLAs.

metrics.name: Throughput_rps
metrics.description: Sustained throughput achieved at a specified concurrency level while maintaining latency SLAs.

metrics.name: CPU_ms_per_min_audio
metrics.unit: CPU-milliseconds per minute of processed audio
metrics.description: Approximate CPU cost normalized by audio length; useful for cost projections in CPU-bound deployments.

metrics.name: GPU_ms_per_min_audio
metrics.unit: GPU-milliseconds per minute of processed audio
metrics.description: Approximate GPU cost normalized by audio length; relevant for GPU-accelerated deployments.

metrics.name: Licensing_cost_per_1k_minutes
metrics.unit: monetary units per 1,000 minutes (e.g., USD/1k minutes)
metrics.description: Estimated marginal licensing or API usage cost per 1,000 minutes of processed audio for any detectors that incur such costs.

metrics.name: Calibrated_Brier_score
metrics.description: Brier score measuring the calibration quality of predicted synthetic probabilities; lower is better.

metrics.name: Adversarial_success_rate
metrics.description: Fraction of adversarial synthetic segments (from D_adv_tools) misclassified as human at a specified operating point.

metrics.name: Domain_perf_ratio_lang
metrics.description: Ratio of AUC_ROC (or 1 – EER) on new-language dataset to the same metric on base-domain dataset; used to quantify domain adaptation effectiveness.

metrics.name: Domain_perf_ratio_channel
metrics.description: Ratio of AUC_ROC (or 1 – EER) on new-channel dataset to the same metric on base-domain dataset.

success_criteria: Ensemble performance: At least one ensemble configuration (e.g., ensemble_weighted_soft or ensemble_stacking_meta_lr) must demonstrate a statistically significant improvement in FNR_at_1pct_FPR and FNR_at_5pct_FPR over the single baseline_cnn_mfcc on D_base_test, with confidence intervals that do not overlap at the chosen significance level.

Domain adaptation retention: After applying domain adaptation strategies, Domain_perf_ratio_lang and Domain_perf_ratio_channel for adapted detectors or ensembles should be at or above a predefined threshold (e.g., ≥0.7 of base-domain performance) while maintaining acceptable FPR on in-domain validation data.

Adversarial robustness: Under WL4_adversarial_tools_eval, at least one ensemble configuration should achieve a lower Adversarial_success_rate than any single constituent detector at equivalent FPR, indicating that ensembles mitigate some tool-specific weaknesses.

Cost–performance trade-offs: The cost-aware analysis under WL5_cost_latency_benchmark should identify at least one Pareto-efficient 'low-cost' and one 'high-security' configuration where no other evaluated configuration simultaneously achieves lower FNR_at_1pct_FPR and lower cost (Licensing_cost_per_1k_minutes + normalized compute costs) at compliant latency.

Reproducibility: Independent reruns of the experiment using the same code, configuration, and environment should produce metrics within a small tolerance band (e.g., ±1% relative for AUC/EER and within defined bounds for latency/throughput) across all workloads.
failure_modes: Data leakage: Accidental inclusion of the same speakers, sessions, or cloned voice identities in both training and evaluation splits, leading to overestimated performance and non-generalizable conclusions.
Inconsistent preprocessing: Divergent audio preprocessing pipelines across detectors (e.g., different resampling or normalization) that confound comparison of detection quality and latency results.
Overfitting ensembles: Meta-learners or weighted ensembles tuned directly on test sets or too-small validation sets, yielding optimistic performance estimates that do not hold for new data.

Unrepresentative adversarial set: Adversarial evaluation relying on a narrow set of cloning tools or unrealistic synthesis parameters that do not reflect actual attacker capabilities in the enterprise context.
Misaligned cost estimates: Using inconsistent pricing models, ignoring fixed overheads, or failing to normalize costs by processed audio duration, leading to misleading cost–performance trade-offs.
Latency benchmarking artifacts: Measuring latency using synthetic loads or different hardware profiles across configurations without proper documentation, making comparisons unreliable.
Regulatory or privacy breach: Using regulated or identifiable customer audio without appropriate approvals, anonymization, or minimization, introducing compliance risk and limiting reproducibility.

Stakeholder misinterpretation: Presenting technical metrics (AUC, EER) without translating their implications into operational risk terms (e.g., expected number of undetected synthetic calls per day), causing poor decision-making on model selection.

hardware.cpu: 64-bit x86_64 processor with at least 8 physical cores (16 vCPUs recommended) and 32 GB RAM.
hardware.gpu: Optional but recommended: at least one modern GPU with CUDA support and 8–16 GB VRAM for efficient training and evaluation of neural detectors.
hardware.storage: Sufficient SSD storage to hold all audio datasets, feature caches, and model artifacts (e.g., 500 GB+ depending on dataset scale).

software.os: Linux distribution (e.g., Ubuntu LTS) or equivalent environment supporting Docker; document exact version.
languages_and_frameworks: Python (e.g., 3.10 or later) as the primary language for the harness.
Deep learning framework (e.g., PyTorch or TensorFlow) for neural detectors.
Audio processing libraries (e.g., librosa, torchaudio, ffmpeg) for standardized pre-processing.
Data handling and analysis tools (e.g., pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn, or equivalents).
software.containerization: Docker or compatible container runtime to package detectors and the evaluation harness for reproducible runs.
software.orchestration_optional: Optional use of a simple orchestration layer (e.g., docker-compose) to manage multiple detector services for ensemble evaluation.
software.monitoring_tools_optional: Lightweight tools for resource measurement such as Linux perf, nvidia-smi, or built-in Python profiling libraries.

suggested_structure: experiments/ch6/ - configuration files, scripts, and documentation for this chapter.
experiments/ch6/config/ - YAML/JSON configs defining detectors, ensembles, and workloads.
experiments/ch6/models/ - scripts to train or load detectors.
experiments/ch6/results/ - structured outputs (metrics, logs, plots) for runs.
data/manifests/ - dataset manifests with checksums and metadata; audio may be stored separately or accessed via secure storage.

access_and_permissions: Ability to store and access audio datasets in compliance with organizational policies.
API keys or credentials for any third-party detection services or voice cloning tools, if they are part of the experiment.
Approvals from internal privacy/compliance stakeholders if real call audio is involved.

run_instructions:
1. Prepare datasets:
   - Assemble or download the base-domain dataset D_base, new-language dataset D_new_lang, new-channel dataset D_new_channel, and adversarial dataset D_adv_tools according to the book's guidance and organizational constraints.
   - For each dataset, create a manifest file listing audio file paths, labels (synthetic/human), language, channel type, and any relevant metadata (e.g., speaker ID, call ID). Store manifests under data/manifests/.
   - Generate stable train/validation/test splits for each dataset, ensuring no leakage across splits; save split indices in structured files (e.g., JSON or CSV) under data/manifests/splits/.
2. Standardize audio preprocessing:
   - Implement a common preprocessing module (e.g., experiments/ch6/harness/preprocess.py) that applies consistent resampling, channel normalization, and feature extraction parameters across detectors where possible.
   - For each detector, document any required deviations (e.g., raw waveform vs. spectrogram input) and integrate them via configuration so the harness remains the single entry point.
3. Implement or integrate detectors:
   - Baseline and supervised detectors: Implement training scripts for baseline_cnn_mfcc and sup_cnn_mfcc_v2 under experiments/ch6/models/, consuming D_base_train and D_base_val splits.
   - Self-supervised detector: Integrate a pre-trained self-supervised speech backbone and implement training of the classification head on D_base_train.
   - Heuristic detector: Implement feature extraction and rule-based scoring logic using the same preprocessing module; calibrate a mapping from heuristic scores to synthetic probabilities using D_base_val.
   - External API detector (if applicable): Implement a thin client in the harness that sends audio segments (or derived features) to the external API and returns synthetic probabilities, handling rate limits and errors.
   - Package each detector either as a callable Python module within the harness or as a containerized microservice with a standardized /predict interface.
4. Train detectors and store artifacts:
   - Run training scripts for all trainable detectors using only the designated training splits; log hyperparameters, training curves, and validation metrics.
   - Save trained model weights, normalization parameters, and calibration objects under experiments/ch6/models/artifacts/ with versioned filenames.
   - For each trained model, run a smoke test on a small subset of D_base_val to verify that inference works and outputs reasonable scores.
5. Configure ensembles and risk-based fusion:
   - Create configuration files (e.g., YAML) under experiments/ch6/config/ defining components and rules for each ensemble: ensemble_majority_vote, ensemble_weighted_soft, ensemble_stacking_meta_lr, and ensemble_risk_tiered_fusion.
   - For stacking: implement cross-validation routines that generate out-of-fold predictions on D_base_train for each base detector; train the meta-learner using these predictions plus optional context features (e.g., channel type), then save the meta-model artifact.
   - For weighted soft voting: optimize weights on D_base_val to minimize a chosen objective (e.g., FNR_at_1pct_FPR) using a simple constrained optimization method (grid search or gradient-free search).
6. Run baseline evaluation (WL1):
   - Use the shared harness (e.g., experiments/ch6/harness/run_eval.py) to evaluate baseline_cnn_mfcc, other individual detectors, and all ensembles on D_base_test.
   - For each model/configuration, compute the full set of detection-quality metrics (AUC_ROC, AUC_PR, EER, FNR_at_1pct_FPR, FNR_at_5pct_FPR, Brier score) and store results in structured JSON or CSV under experiments/ch6/results/WL1/.
   - Optionally, generate plots (ROC, PR) and calibration curves for documentation, stored under experiments/ch6/results/WL1/plots/.
7. Apply and evaluate domain adaptation (WL2 and WL3):
   - For language adaptation: select a small labeled subset of D_new_lang_train according to the defined budget. Apply the lang_specific_finetune strategy to train adapted versions of baseline_cnn_mfcc and selfsup_embedding_classifier; keep original models unchanged for comparison.
   - For channel adaptation: apply channel_calibration_only to adjust thresholds or calibration parameters based on D_new_channel_val without altering model weights.
   - Evaluate both original and adapted detectors, as well as ensembles built from them, on D_new_lang_test and D_new_channel_test using the harness, saving metrics under experiments/ch6/results/WL2/ and WL3/ respectively.
   - Compute Domain_perf_ratio_lang and Domain_perf_ratio_channel and store them alongside core metrics.
8. Conduct adversarial evaluation (WL4):
   - Generate or acquire synthetic audio from multiple voice cloning tools with varying parameters as described; ensure manifests record the tool and settings used for each segment.
   - Evaluate all detectors and ensembles on D_adv_tools using the shared harness.
   - Compute Adversarial_success_rate at chosen operating points (e.g., thresholds that yield 1% and 5% FPR on D_base_val) and store results under experiments/ch6/results/WL4/.
   - Analyze tool-specific and transformation-specific breakdowns (e.g., by cloning tool, codec, noise level) if dataset size permits.
9. Benchmark latency and cost (WL5):
   - For selected configurations (e.g., baseline_cnn_mfcc, ensemble_majority_vote, ensemble_weighted_soft, ensemble_stacking_meta_lr, config_low_cost, config_high_security), run dedicated latency and throughput benchmarks using the harness in benchmark mode.
   - Use a realistic mix of audio segments reflecting deployment conditions; run at one or more concurrency levels (e.g., 1, 10, 50 parallel requests) and record Latency_p50, Latency_p95, Throughput_rps, CPU_ms_per_min_audio, and GPU_ms_per_min_audio.
   - Combine compute usage with estimated infrastructure pricing and any vendor licensing fees to compute Licensing_cost_per_1k_minutes where applicable; store all results under experiments/ch6/results/WL5/.
10. Analyze trade-offs and document for stakeholders:
   - Using the collected metrics across workloads, plot or tabulate cost–performance curves (e.g., FNR_at_1pct_FPR vs. total cost) to identify Pareto-efficient configurations.
   - Summarize, in a human-readable report (e.g., Markdown or PDF under experiments/ch6/results/summary/), which configurations are best suited for low-, medium-, and high-risk call flows, explicitly stating detection performance, latency, and cost implications.
   - Translate key technical metrics into operational impact estimates relevant to the book’s enterprise audience (e.g., expected number of undetected synthetic calls per 100k calls at current channel mix).
11. Verify reproducibility:
   - Re-run a subset of evaluations (e.g., WL1 and WL4) from a fresh environment (or by a separate team member) using the same code and configs.
   - Compare resulting metrics to original runs; if discrepancies exceed defined tolerances, investigate and document causes (e.g., non-deterministic GPU operations, environment drift) and update the harness or documentation accordingly.
12. Archive and tag experiment state:
   - Commit all configuration files, code changes, and manifests to the repository under a dedicated branch or tag corresponding to this experiment (e.g., ch6-v1).
   - Store model artifacts and result files in a structured, discoverable manner, with README files capturing environment details, dataset versions, and any known caveats.
   - Optionally, publish anonymized metric summaries and harness code as part of the public repository to support readers reproducing the experiments.

evidence_schema.description: Schema for recording raw and aggregated results from each experimental run so that they can be analyzed, compared, and communicated to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

run_id.description: Unique identifier for a single execution of the harness for a given model configuration and workload (e.g., UUID).

timestamp_utc.description: Start time of the run in UTC.

code_version.description: Information about the code and configuration versions used in the run.

git_commit.description: Git commit hash of the repository at run time.

config_files.description: List of configuration file paths used for this run.

environment.description: Description of the hardware and software environment used during the run.

dl_framework.description: Name and version of deep learning framework.

other_libraries.description: Optional list of key library versions.

dataset_id.description: Identifier of the dataset split used in the run (e.g., D_base_test, D_new_lang_test, D_adv_tools).

workload_id.description: Identifier of the workload scenario (e.g., WL1_base_domain_eval).

model_config.description: Details about the detector or ensemble being evaluated.

detector_id.description: ID of the primary detector or ensemble (e.g., baseline_cnn_mfcc, ensemble_stacking_meta_lr).

component_detectors.description: List of component detector IDs for ensembles; empty or omitted for single detectors.

hyperparameters.description: Key hyperparameters for the model (e.g., learning rate, batch size, architecture choices).

fusion_strategy.description: Description of fusion strategy (e.g., hard_voting, soft_voting, stacking, risk_based) for ensembles; optional otherwise.

domain_adaptation.description: Description of any domain adaptation or calibration applied before this run.

metric_confidence_intervals.description: Optional confidence intervals or variability estimates for key metrics.

aggregation_level.description: Indicates whether metrics are computed at segment level, call level, or both.

notes.description: Free-form field for run-specific annotations (e.g., anomalies observed, partial failures, deviations from standard protocol).
